summary: _fmtio.py is well-factored: shared codegen (_emit_variadic_call), shared arg validation/promotion helpers, and a single exec'd-source impl builder eliminate most cross-binding duplication, and it correctly composes the canonical get_unicode_data_p / array_data_p primitives rather than reinventing them. Only low-severity design nits remain: duplicated %n-rejection logic across the two dual-mode entry points, the scanf arg-type check inlined twice instead of a helper paralleling _validate_writer_arg_type, and a genuinely-unused get_unicode_data_p argument threaded into the sscanf overload's impl builder.

findings.title: %n-rejection logic duplicated across _reject_percent_n_or_raise and _reject_percent_n_in_python
findings.claim: Two functions implement the identical %n detection: same `_PERCENT_N_RE`, the same `stripped = fmt.replace('%%', '\x00\x00')` pre-pass, and a near-identical message body. They differ only in the raised exception type (TypingError vs ValueError). The %%-stripping line and the regex search are copy-pasted; a future change to the directive grammar (or the %% handling) must be made in lockstep in both places or the @njit and pure-Python modes silently diverge on what they reject.
findings.evidence: _reject_percent_n_or_raise (237-253): `stripped = fmt_str.replace('%%', '\x00\x00')` then `if _PERCENT_N_RE.search(stripped):`. _reject_percent_n_in_python (511-512): `stripped = fmt.replace('%%', '\x00\x00')` then `if _PERCENT_N_RE.search(stripped):`. The detection half is byte-for-byte identical; only the raise differs.
findings.recommendation: Extract the detection into a single private predicate, e.g. `def _has_percent_n(fmt): return bool(_PERCENT_N_RE.search(fmt.replace('%%', '\x00\x00')))`, and have both wrappers call it and raise their own exception type. Keeps the two distinct error types (the deliberate dual-mode split) while making the grammar single-sourced. Local, low-risk.

findings.title: sscanf arg-type check (ty != intp) inlined in four places instead of a shared validator
findings.claim: The writer family (printf/fprintf/snprintf) routes all per-arg type validation through the shared `_validate_writer_arg_type` helper, but sscanf hand-inlines the same `if ty != intp: raise TypingError(...args[{i}] must be intp (output pointer)...)` loop in both its @intrinsic (401-405) and its @overload (677-681). The two inlined copies must be kept message-consistent by hand, breaking the otherwise-uniform 'one validator, called from both the typing and overload layers' design used by every sibling binding.
findings.evidence: _sscanf_intrinsic 401-405: `for i, ty in enumerate(tuple(args_ty)): if ty != intp: raise TypingError(f"sscanf: args[{i}] must be intp (output pointer), got {ty!r}")`. _overload_sscanf 677-681 repeats the identical loop/message. Compare the writer family which calls `_validate_writer_arg_type(name, i, ty)` from both layers (e.g. 316-317 intrinsic, 548 overload).
findings.recommendation: Add a `_validate_scanf_arg_type(name, idx, ty)` private helper (mirroring `_validate_writer_arg_type`) and call it from both sscanf layers, single-sourcing the intp-only contract and its error message.

findings.title: sscanf overload threads a get_unicode_data_p argument that the generated impl never references
findings.claim: `_overload_sscanf` passes `_get_unicode_data_p_lazy()` into `_build_overload_impl`, but for sscanf every arg is intp so `_build_args_tuple_expr_from_starargs` emits only `args[i]` index expressions and never a `get_unicode_data_p(...)` call. The helper is therefore placed into the exec namespace (`ns = {"_intr": ..., "get_unicode_data_p": ...}`) but is unreferenced dead surface for the scanf path, and the call site even self-documents this with the comment `# unused (no UnicodeType in args)`.
findings.evidence: _overload_sscanf 682-685: `impl = _build_overload_impl("sscanf", ["buf", "fmt"], args, _sscanf_intrinsic, _get_unicode_data_p_lazy(),  # unused (no UnicodeType in args))`. _build_overload_impl 465: `ns = {"_intr": intrinsic_callable, "get_unicode_data_p": get_unicode_data_p}` — the name is bound but the generated `src` for an all-intp arg list (from _build_args_tuple_expr_from_starargs, 444-447) only emits `args[{i}]`, never `get_unicode_data_p(args[{i}])`.
findings.recommendation: Either make the `get_unicode_data_p` parameter of `_build_overload_impl` optional (default None, only inject into ns when provided) and pass nothing from sscanf, or accept it as harmless and leave the explanatory comment. Pure cleanup; no behavior change.
